whatIsThisScreen.heading: What this screen is
whatIsThisScreen.body: A summary of the overall state of your finances: how much liquid money you have, how much you owe on credit cards, how close you are to your budget limit, and which payments are coming up.

cardsAbove.heading: The cards up top
cardsAbove.body: <0>Liquidity</0> adds up the balance of your cash/bank-type accounts (not credit cards). <2>Revolving debt</2> is what you owe on active credit cards, with its average APR. <4>Month budget</4> and <6>week budget</6> show what percentage you've spent against what was budgeted — the color changes from green to orange to red depending on how close you are to the limit. As soon as you generate the current month's report (Reports → Generate), two more cards appear: <8>Month income</8> and <10>Month expenses</10>, each compared against the previous month.

upcomingPayments.heading: Upcoming payments
upcomingPayments.body: Combines your active recurring expenses (Netflix, rent, etc.) with debt payments due in the next 7 days. If something is due in 3 days or less, it shows as a notice above the cards.

netWorthAndDebts.heading: Net worth and active debts
netWorthAndDebts.body: The net worth line uses your generated monthly reports (Reports → Generate); if a month has no report, no point appears for it. Each debt's progress compares the current balance against the original amount — it doesn't distinguish principal from interest, it's a quick visual reference.

help.readOnlyTip: This screen is read-only — to record transactions use Transactions, and to see the detail of each item go to its specific page (the "See all →" links take you straight there).

whatIsThisScreen.heading: What this screen is
whatIsThisScreen.body: Your real accounts: banks, cash, and credit cards. The summary above (Assets, Liabilities, Net worth) is calculated by adding up the balance of all of them.

accountTypes.heading: Account types
accountTypes.body: When creating an account you choose between bank, savings, cash, and credit card. The first three are money you have available; the card is a liability (what you owe) -- not the same as a Debt: formal or informal loans live separately, in Debts.

creditCards.heading: Credit cards
creditCards.body: Besides the name and balance, a credit card stores credit limit, interest rate, billing day, and payment due day — the last two feed the billing cycle you see in the account's detail. The "Pay card" button (here or in Transactions) records the payment as a real transfer from any of your other accounts. If you buy something in interest-free installments, mark it when recording the expense and you'll see the progress ("installments paid/total") right in the card's history.

logo.heading: Logo and customization
logo.body: You can upload a photo/logo to identify the account at a glance (it's cropped and fitted to a square automatically) and choose a color that's used in charts and lists throughout the app.

transactions.heading: Account transactions
transactions.body: When you select an account on the left, you see its transaction history on the right, with an In/Out filter and search.

reconcile.heading: Reconcile balance
reconcile.body: Available on bank/savings accounts. You enter what you actually have (counted, or from your statement) and the app records an adjustment transaction for the difference — unlike editing the "Initial balance", this does show up as a visible transaction in your history.

help.tip: Lending money to someone, or being lent money, doesn't create an account here — it lives in Debts, separate from your real accounts, no matter how many people are involved.

confirmDelete.title: Delete transaction
confirmDelete.message: Delete the transaction "{{description}}"? This action cannot be undone.

overview.heading: What this screen is
overview.body: The full history of your activity: income, expenses, transfers and loans. You can filter by account, type, date or text, and see the same data as a calendar on the right — clicking a day filters the list automatically.

newTransaction.heading: + New transaction
newTransaction.body: Record income, an expense, or a transfer between two of your accounts. For income/expense you only pick account, category and amount — the app resolves the accounting counterpart on its own, you never have to choose it. If the expense is on a credit card, you can mark it "Interest-free installments?" — that doesn't create a separate debt, it just tags that purchase so you can see its progress in Accounts.

payCard.heading: Pay credit card
payCard.body: Only shows up if you have at least one credit card registered. Records a real transfer from any of your other accounts to the card — it's the same button available in the account's detail view, offered here so you don't have to go to Accounts first.

sharedExpense.heading: Shared expense
sharedExpense.body1: For when you paid for something that's only partly your expense (e.g. a group dinner). You record the full charge to your account/card, how much is really yours, and how much each person owes — their share becomes a balance in your favor in Debts ("They owe me"), not your expense.
sharedExpense.body2: Because it involves more than two internal movements, a shared expense can no longer be edited once created (only deleted) — double check the amounts before saving it.

help.tip: Lending money directly (with no purchase involved), or someone lending to you, no longer lives here — it's in <1>Debts</1>, along with everything else that involves owing money in either direction.

whatIsThisScreen.heading: What is this screen
whatIsThisScreen.body: Your profile and account preferences — not settings for one particular screen, but for the whole app: how you look, how you identify yourself, and how you sign in.

profilePhoto.heading: Profile photo
profilePhoto.body: If you signed in with Google, your photo is imported automatically the first time. You can upload your own whenever you want — once you upload one manually, a future Google login won't replace it anymore.

themeNotificationsPayCycle.heading: Theme, language, notifications and pay cycle
themeNotificationsPayCycle.body: The theme (dark/light) and language are saved to your account, not this browser -- if you sign in from another device, they look the same. The pay cycle (weekly/biweekly/monthly) is what Dashboard and Budget use to calculate the current week/period.

debtTrouble.heading: Debt trouble
debtTrouble.body: Off by default on purpose — turn it on only if you genuinely have a past-due loan or debt you're not paying. It enables a separate section in Debts and gives the AI Advisor context to help you analyze how to get out of it.

googleAccount.heading: Google account
googleAccount.body: If you linked Google, you can unlink it here — but only if your account also has a password; otherwise you'd be left with no way to sign in.

eraseData.heading: Delete data
eraseData.body: To start fresh without losing your account: two quick buttons ("everything except accounts" or "absolutely everything") and a list to delete only specific categories — for example, just transactions, or just the AI Advisor history. Deleting bank accounts also deletes your transactions and recurring items, since they depend on the account existing.

help.tip: Deleting your account is permanent: it closes all your sessions and disables access. "Delete data" is different — your login stays intact, only what you choose gets deleted.

correctBalanceForm.confirmMessage: You're about to change the balance of "{{name}}" from {{from}} to {{to}} directly -- it doesn't register any payment or modify existing ones, it only adjusts the number. Continue?

whatIsThisScreen.heading: What this screen is
whatIsThisScreen.body: Everything that involves owing money, in either direction: personal loans, payroll loans, store credit, or something as informal as lending a friend $100 or your grandfather lending you $100,000. Credit cards don't live here -- they're paid off and you see the progress of your installment purchases from Accounts. The tab above switches between <0>I owe</0> and <1>Owed to me</1> — same model, same screen, only who owes whom changes.

addDebt.heading: Add debt
addDebt.body: Register a debt with its full plan: amount, payment frequency and, optionally, which account the cash moved from/to when it originated. Under "I owe" you also choose the type (personal loan, informal, etc.) — under "Owed to me" it's always an informal loan.

unplannedDebt.heading: Unplanned debt
unplannedDebt.body1: For when you don't have the details clear yet — just a name and an amount. It never moves money out of any account. Once you know how it's going to be paid, you "activate" it with a plan (and there you can say which account the cash came from/went into, if applicable).
unplannedDebt.body2: This section is off by default — it only appears if you turn on "I have a debt with payment problems" in Settings. Once turned on, the AI advisor can also see these debts and help you analyze how to pay them off.
steps: Unplanned debt: save the name and the amount, nothing more.
Once you decide how to pay it, activate it with an amount/frequency/account.
From then on it behaves like any other debt.

registerPayment.heading: Register payment / collection
registerPayment.body: Lowers the outstanding balance and moves real money to/from the account you choose — it's a real transaction, not just a number changing. Under "Owed to me" it's called "Register collection" (you're getting paid), under "I owe" it's "Register payment".

correctBalance.heading: Correct balance
correctBalance.body: Adjusts the outstanding balance directly to what it really is today, without registering payment by payment — meant for when you're loading old history and just need to leave the final number correct. Unlike "Register payment", it doesn't move money out of any account or affect payments already registered.

help.tip: Lending or borrowing isn't an expense or income — your total net worth doesn't change, it just moves from one account to another (or to this list, if it doesn't have an associated account yet).

setLimits.pastMonthNote: This affects the current month, not the past month you're viewing.

whatIsThisScreen.heading: What this screen is
whatIsThisScreen.body: How much you plan to spend per variable expense category (food, transportation, etc.) each month, against what you've actually spent — separate from your committed fixed expenses (debts, recurring items).

settingLimit.heading: Setting a limit
settingLimit.body: You set a monthly cap on a category. If you haven't set a limit on any category, nothing shows up in the breakdown — it's optional, category by category.

limitSuggestion.heading: Limit suggestion
limitSuggestion.body: When your average spending over the last 3 months in a category differs from its current limit, it's flagged for you and you can apply it with one click — no need to calculate it yourself.

available.heading: Available
available.body: Estimated income minus fixed committed minus spent. If it turns red (negative), you've already gone over what you can spend this month.

navigatingPastMonths.heading: Browsing past months
navigatingPastMonths.body: Use the arrows next to the month to review how you did in previous months. The weekly view and the limit alert only apply to the current month — a closed month no longer has a "current week".

categoryArrow.heading: Arrow per category
categoryArrow.body: Compares this category's spending against the previous month. Red pointing up if you spent more than 5% more, green pointing down if you spent less — no arrow if it's roughly the same.

help.fixedCommittedTip: "Fixed committed" is your active debts and recurring items — money you already know you're going to spend, which is why it doesn't compete with the variable budget above.

categories.title: Categories
categories.deleteConfirmMessage: Delete "{{name}}"? Transactions using it will be left uncategorized. This action cannot be undone.
categories.deactivateConfirmMessage: Deactivate "{{name}}" for you? It will stop appearing in your list and your transactions using it will be left uncategorized -- you can reactivate it whenever you want, this only affects you.
categories.iconSearchPlaceholder: Search across all 8 categories… e.g. gas, coffee

help.whatIsThisBody: The categories you use to classify your income and expenses. Each card shows how much you've received or spent in that category during the current month.
help.systemVsYoursBody: Categories marked System come predefined and can't be edited or deleted (they guarantee there's always somewhere to classify a transaction), but you can deactivate them for yourself with the crossed-out eye icon if you don't use them — they stop appearing in your list and you can reactivate them whenever you want from the section below; it doesn't affect other users. Categories you create can be renamed, have their color/icon changed, or be deleted with the "×".
help.subcategoriesBody: Top-level expense categories can have subcategories (e.g. "Restaurants" and "Groceries" inside "Food and Drink") — expand the category to see them or add a new one. Only one level is allowed: a subcategory can't have subcategories of its own. The monthly budget is always defined on the parent category; what you spend on its subcategories adds up there automatically. The bar below each card's amount compares that direct expense against its subcategories, each with its own color.
help.transactionsBody: When you deactivate a system category or delete one of your own (trash icon), the transactions that had it assigned are left uncategorized (they aren't deleted, and the action isn't blocked) — you can recategorize them later if needed.
help.tip: You never choose an accounting account when using a category in a transaction — the system resolves it internally on its own. Here you only manage the catalog of names.

form.utilityHint: Essential utilities alert daily starting the first day they go unconfirmed.

creditCardCommitments.heading: What your cards already owe by the next cutoff
creditCardCommitments.hint: Monthly installments from interest-free purchases + what you've already spent in each card's open cycle. Informational only -- it isn't included in "Committed / month" above.

listSection.heading: Recurring services and income
listSection.empty: No recurring items with this status.

whatIsThisScreen.heading: What this screen is
whatIsThisScreen.body: Expenses and income that repeat on a fixed cycle — services, utilities (power, water, internet) and recurring income like payroll. Subscriptions (Netflix, Spotify, etc.) have their own dedicated page.

unconfirmed.heading: Unconfirmed
unconfirmed.body: As a recurring item's date approaches, the system automatically prepares the movement as a draft — it shows up above so you can confirm it (it's recorded as-is) or reject it (it didn't happen, it's discarded) before it counts as a real transaction.

editPauseCancel.heading: Edit / Pause / Cancel / Resume
editPauseCancel.body: Edit changes amount, frequency, account, category, urgency, or next charge date without losing the item's history — use it when your rent goes up or a service's amount changes. Pause temporarily stops automatic generation without losing the configuration. Cancel retires it for good. All of them can be resumed later.

upcomingAndBreakdown.heading: Upcoming payments and breakdown by category
upcomingAndBreakdown.body: "Upcoming payments" are the ones falling in the next 7 days, to help plan your pay period. The breakdown by category splits "Committed / month" (same total, same scope: no subscriptions or income) so you can see where that money goes.

cardDebts.heading: What your cards already owe
cardDebts.body: Only shows up if you have at least one credit card. It adds up the monthly installments from your active interest-free purchases (fixed, has to be paid no matter what) plus what you've already spent in each card's open cycle (variable, keeps rising until it closes). It's informational only -- it isn't added to "Committed / month" above, because that expense was already counted in the budget for the month it happened; adding it here too would count it twice.

help.tip: Alert urgency (normal/high/critical) controls how insistent the reminder is before the charge date — it doesn't affect the amount or the date itself. "Essential utilities" are the exception: they alert daily starting the first day they go unconfirmed, regardless of the urgency you set.

renewalsSection.heading: Upcoming renewals (7 days)
renewalsSection.empty: Nothing renewing in the next 7 days.

listSection.heading: All your subscriptions
listSection.emptyActive: You don't have any active subscriptions.
listSection.emptyPaused: You don't have any paused subscriptions.
listSection.emptyCancelled: You don't have any cancelled subscriptions.

whatIsThisScreen.heading: What this screen is
whatIsThisScreen.body: Your subscriptions (streaming, software, memberships) separate from other recurring items — so you can see at a glance how much they cost you per month in total, without mixing them with rent or utilities.

monthlyCommitment.heading: Monthly commitment
monthlyCommitment.body: Since not all of them charge every month (some are annual or biweekly), the total converts each frequency to its monthly equivalent so the sum makes sense.

editPauseCancel.heading: Edit / Pause / Cancel / Resume
editPauseCancel.body: Edit changes amount, frequency, account, category, or next charge date without losing the history — use it when the price goes up (happens often with streaming and software). Pause stops the automatic charge without losing the configuration. Cancel is permanent. Both can be reverted.

activeSince.heading: Active for N months
activeSince.body: A passive reminder of how long a subscription has been active — starting at 12 months it flags it, so every now and then you ask yourself whether you're really still using it.

upcomingRenewals.heading: Upcoming renewals
upcomingRenewals.body: The ones charging in the next 7 days, so no charge catches you off guard.

help.tip: The amount is automatically recorded in Transactions when the charge date arrives — it first shows up as pending confirmation in Recurring.

insights.title: Insights
insights.noActiveInsights: No active insights. Generate new ones or ask the AI Advisor to save a plan.

whatIsThisScreen.heading: What this screen is
whatIsThisScreen.body: Automatic observations about your finances based on your real data (spending, budget, debts) — a detected pattern, an alert, a suggestion. Up to 10 active at a time.

generateInsights.heading: Generate insights
generateInsights.body: Runs the analysis on your current situation and creates new insights if it finds something worth pointing out. They're also created automatically when you ask the AI Advisor to save a plan.

markResolvedDismiss.heading: Mark resolved / Dismiss
markResolvedDismiss.body: Resolved is for when you've already addressed what it said. Dismiss is for when a particular one doesn't interest you. Both remove it from the active list and it stays in the history below.

viewReviews.heading: View reviews
viewReviews.body: While an insight is still active, it re-evaluates itself (with your data at the time) on each review date, and the AI says whether your situation improved, worsened, or stayed the same — with a comparison of your key numbers (net worth, financial health, committed monthly) against those from when it was created.

help.tip: Priority (high/medium/low) reflects how urgent it is — it isn't tied to any automatic action, it's just so you can decide what to attend to first.

whatIsThisScreen.heading: What this screen is
whatIsThisScreen.body: Reports for periods that are already closed (previous month or year) — unlike Budget/Dashboard, which are real-time, a report is a frozen "snapshot" of a period that already ended, with analysis generated over those numbers.

generateMonthYear.heading: Generate previous month/year
generateMonthYear.body: Reports aren't created on their own — you generate them whenever you want to see them. A yearly report needs the monthly reports for that year to already exist.

regenerateReport.heading: Regenerate a report
regenerateReport.body: The icon next to the period selector recalculates the report you're viewing from scratch, with your current transactions — useful if you generated a report before loading old history and it came out nearly empty. For a yearly report, it also recalculates the 12 months of that year.

incomeExpenseAll.heading: Income / Expenses / All
incomeExpenseAll.body: Filters both the featured category and the "Points for this period" (AI-generated observations about that specific report).

netWorthHistory.heading: Net worth — history
netWorthHistory.body: Combines all your generated monthly reports to draw your net worth line over time — the more months you generate, the more complete it looks.

savingsRateDtiColors.heading: Savings rate and DTI colors
savingsRateDtiColors.body: Savings rate: red if negative (you spent more than you earned), orange below 10%, green from there up. DTI (debt/income): orange from 20%, red from 36% — the classic "risk zone" threshold in personal finance.

help.tip: Savings rate and DTI are indicators for the closed report, not the current month — for that, use the "Current month" note at the bottom of the page.

sidebar.disclaimer: The advisor uses this same financial snapshot and several tools to answer with your real data, and can create accounts, debts, recurring items, or transactions if you ask it to log them (it will always confirm with you before saving anything).

dialog.title: More ways to bring in data
dialog.promptDescription: Copy it and paste it into the conversation where you've been tracking your finances (ChatGPT, Gemini, etc.). That AI will give you back a summary you can paste here in the chat.

whatIsThisScreen.heading: What this screen is
whatIsThisScreen.body: An AI chat that sees your real financial situation (accounts, debts, budget, recent transactions) and answers using that as context — these aren't generic answers.

suggestions.heading: Suggestions
suggestions.body: The common-question buttons are just a starting point — you can ask whatever you want in the text box below.

clearHistory.heading: Clear history
clearHistory.body: The trash icon deletes the saved conversation — useful for starting fresh, it doesn't affect your financial data, only the chat.

remainingQueriesToday.heading: Queries left today
remainingQueriesToday.body: There's a daily question limit to control AI costs. The number next to "Connected" tells you how many you have left — it resets every day.

historicalData.heading: Bringing in historical data
historicalData.body: The 📎 next to the message attaches account statements as PDF (works even if they're password-protected — type it once for the whole batch) — the assistant logs regular charges and installment purchases (MSI) at their full amount only once, without duplicating when that same installment shows up again in later statements. Marking a purchase as an installment plan to see its progress in Accounts is a separate step you do yourself when reviewing the transaction — the assistant doesn't do it on its own. The "+" button has two more ways in: uploading a pre-filled Excel file, or copying a prompt to paste into another AI (ChatGPT, Gemini) and bring back an already-structured summary.

help.tip: If you ask it to save a plan or recommendation, it creates it as an Insight you can view later in that section (we'll let you know right there in the chat when it happens). It can also create accounts, debts, recurring items, or log transactions if you dictate the details or attach a PDF — it always summarizes what it's about to save and waits for your confirmation before doing it. It can't edit or delete anything that already exists.

confirmDeactivateUser.message: Deactivate "{{name}}" ({{email}})? They won't be able to log in until you reactivate them.

tempPasswordDialog.title: Temporary password — {{name}}
tempPasswordDialog.description: Share it with the user now outside the app — it can't be shown again.

dialog.notifyMessage: {{name}} will get a notification about this change. You can add a note explaining why -- it's optional, but it helps the response not feel cold.
dialog.notePlaceholder: E.g. We added it to the Q4 roadmap, or: it doesn't fit the app's current focus.

whatIsThisScreen.heading: What this screen is
whatIsThisScreen.body: All the alerts the app has generated for you: reports ready, new insights, budget or debt alerts, cards coming due, and pending payment reminders.

readingNotifications.heading: Reading notifications
readingNotifications.body: A colored dot marks what you haven't read. Clicking a notification marks it as read; "Mark all as read" does it for all of them at once.

help.tip: Each notification's icon and color indicate its type (debt, budget, report, insight) — you don't need to open it to know what it's about.

goals.title: Goals
goals.comingSoon: Coming soon — savings goals (for example, a down payment or an emergency fund) aren't a backend module yet. Once it's built, you'll be able to set a target amount, a monthly contribution, and see a projection of when you'll reach it.
